about: What each of the six fire questions is about, fixed before any passage was labelled. The guide is what the labelling followed; the phrases are what scripts/build_topics.mjs gives the site's small language model when its search is measured against the labels. Written with AI assistance (Claude Code, Anthropic).
rules: A passage can belong to several questions, or to none.
Each label must quote the words in the passage that justify it; the build checks the quote word for word.

Label what the passage is about, not what it could be relevant to. General combustion science (flame chemistry, soot formation, droplet burning rates) belongs to no question unless it touches the guide.

tested.guide: Fire or combustion in air with more oxygen than normal air, or at reduced total pressure, or spacecraft atmospheres planned with such conditions. Varying oxygen only at or below normal air does not count.
phrases: combustion in oxygen-enriched air at reduced pressure
burning at elevated oxygen concentration above normal air
spacecraft cabin atmosphere with higher oxygen and lower pressure for exploration missions

materials.guide: Whether solid materials burn: ignition, flame spread or burning of fabrics, plastics, paper, foams or other solid samples, including burners built to imitate burning solids.
phrases: flammability of solid materials such as fabrics and plastics
flame spread over a solid fuel sample
ignition and burning of spacecraft cabin materials

earth-test.guide: Comparisons of how materials or fires burn in normal gravity and in low gravity, made for fire safety or material selection, or ground-based flammability tests and standards and whether they hold in space.
phrases: comparing material flammability in normal gravity and in microgravity
ground-based material flammability screening test for spacecraft
whether tests on Earth predict how materials burn in space

put-out.guide: How a flame is put out or goes out: suppressant gases, removing the airflow, extinguishment, or the limits (oxygen, flow, size) below which a flame cannot survive.
phrases: extinguishing a fire with suppressant gases such as carbon dioxide or helium
conditions under which a flame goes out

detect.guide: Noticing a fire: smoke detectors, gas or particle sensors, or the properties of smoke and particles from fires studied for detection. Soot chemistry inside a flame does not count by itself.
phrases: smoke particles produced by a fire and how they are detected
fire detection and smoke detectors on spacecraft
gas and particle sensors for early fire warning

gravity.guide: Fire in partial gravity, such as on the Moon or Mars, or at gravity levels between weightlessness and normal gravity. Weightlessness alone does not count.
phrases: fire in partial gravity on the Moon or Mars
flames at gravity levels between weightlessness and normal gravity
